title: Starship flight 15 powers to orbit—setting up a possible catch on Saturday
author: Eric Berger
summary_long: STARBASE, Texas—Starship lifted off right on schedule Friday from South Texas, making its 15th test flight in more than three years. The largely successful launch took place in the early evening; as the massive rocket rose into the atmosphere, the Sun sank toward the western horizon. Conditions were ideal for the launch, with the atmospheric winds so calm the rocket’s white plume did not dissipate for many minutes. id: bigtech:windows 0day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers:2026-11-13T16:26:32.000Z
title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
author: Dan Goodin
summary_long: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System, which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System. TURNING A WINDOWS DEFENSE AGAINST ITSELF The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions. Source: arstechnica.com. Date: 2026-11-13. title: James Webb telescope finds ice older than the star it orbits
author: Jacek Krywko
summary_long: Beta Pictoris is a young star, roughly 20 million years old, and located about 64 light-years away from Earth. It is surrounded by a vast disk of dust and rubble where planets are still forming—astronomers have already found three. In a new Science study, a team led by Sarah Betti, an astronomer at the Space Telescope Science Institute in Baltimore, used the James Webb Space Telescope to look for ice in this disk. Researchers found both water and carbon dioxide ice. Source: arstechnica.com. Date: 2026-11-14. Why it matters: outline likely impact on technology, business, or society.
